problems.title: Difference from a reciprocal
problems.question: By how much does2.5 exceed its reciprocal?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: The difference is2.5−0.4=2.1.

problems.title: Smallest sum of distinct composites
problems.question: Find the smallest number expressible as a sum of three distinct composite positive integers.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: The three smallest composite positive integers are4,6,8.
steps: Any three distinct composites have sum at least4+6+8=18,and this sum is attainable.

problems.title: Pair all divisors of a prime power
problems.question: Find the product of all positive divisors of5¹⁰⁰.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: The divisors are5⁰,5¹,…,5¹⁰⁰;their exponent sum is100·101/2=5050.
steps: Their product is5⁵⁰⁵⁰. Equivalently,pair complementary divisors whose product is5¹⁰⁰.

problems.title: An internal and an external angle bisector
problems.question: AE bisects angleA internally and CE bisects angleC externally in triangleABC. If AEC=22°,find B.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: The smaller angle between these two bisectors is B/2.
steps: For a direct angle chase,the triangleACE has angleA=A/2 and angleC=90°+C/2.
Its remaining angle is90°−(A+C)/2=B/2. Hence B=44°.

problems.title: Use the incenter on a circle
problems.question: A circle through A,C and triangleABC’s incenterI meets BC atD. If ADC=155°,find B.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: $\angle AIC=90^\circ+B/2$. In the shown cyclic configuration,I andD lie on the same side of chordAC.
steps: Their inscribed angles subtendingAC are equal,so90°+B/2=155°.
Thus B/2=65° and B=130°.

problems.title: Difference of squares gives a sum
problems.question: Given x²−y²=28 and x−y=4,find(x+y)².
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: Thus4(x+y)=28,so x+y=7. Its square is49.

problems.title: Compare exponents with the same base
problems.question: Given(2^x)^y=4^x and(4^y)^x=8^y,with x<y,find x+y.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Equal powers of2 give xy=2x and2xy=3y.
steps: Thus x(y−2)=0 and y(2x−3)=0. If either variable is zero,both are zero,violating x<y.
Otherwise y=2,x=3/2,which satisfies x<y. Sum=7/2=3.5.

problems.title: Sum of squares of quadratic roots
problems.question: For roots x₁,x₂ of x²−3x−19=0,find x₁²+x₂².
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: The result is9+38=47.

problems.title: Both radicals must be defined
problems.question: How many roots has √(x²+5x)·√(x²+3x)=0?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Domain requires x(x+5)≥0 and x(x+3)≥0,so x≤−5 or x≥0.
steps: The candidate zeros are0,−5,−3. The input−3 makes the first radicand negative.
Only0 and−5 remain,so there are two roots.

problems.title: Two equilateral triangles attached to a square
problems.question: ABCD is a square;AED and DEF are equilateral as shown. Find CFA.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: The direction of FA forms210° with the positive horizontal axis. The vector FC=(−1/2,1−√3/2) forms165°.
For the second direction,use(1−√3/2)/(1/2)=2−√3=tan15°.
Their smaller difference is210°−165°=45°.

problems.title: A cyclic angle transfers to a parallelogram
problems.question: A circle through C,D of parallelogramABCD meets AD atE and AC atF. If FEA=28°,find CAB.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: EA and ED are opposite rays,so FED=152°. Opposite cyclic angles give FCD=28°.
steps: Since CF lies on CA and CD is parallel toAB,the angle FCD equals CAB. Therefore CAB=28°.

problems.title: Profit is revenue minus cost
problems.question: Selling at twice the planned price triples a merchant’s profit. How many times the planned profit results at four times the price?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Let planned price p,cost c. Then2p−c=3(p−c).
steps: This gives c=p/2. Planned profit is p/2;profit at price4p is4p−p/2=7p/2.
The ratio is(7p/2)/(p/2)=7.

problems.title: Relate group totals to their averages
problems.question: Girls’ average score is20% above boys’;boys’ total is60% above girls’. How many percent more boys participated?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Total score=number×average. Let averages be b and1.2b.
steps: If counts areN_b,N_g,thenN_b b=1.6N_g(1.2b). ThusN_b=1.92N_g.
There were92% more boys.

problems.title: A ratio from a linear relation
problems.question: If x−y=(2/3)(x+y),what fraction of x is y?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: Thus x=5y and y/x=1/5=0.2 when the requested ratio is defined.
problems.note: The zero pair also satisfies the equation but makes y/x undefined. The ratio question implicitly takes x≠0.

problems.title: Inradius as a fraction of the hypotenuse
problems.question: In an isosceles right triangle,what fraction of the hypotenuse is the inradius?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Legs l,l,hypotenusel√2; $r=(l+l-l\sqrt2)/2$.
steps: Divide by l√2 to get r/c=(√2−1)/2. Rationalising the listed equivalent form gives1/(2+√8).

problems.title: Principal square roots produce absolute values
problems.question: Simplify √(5−2√6)+√((√3−5)²).
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: The first radical is√3−√2. The second is5−√3 because√3<5.
Adding gives5−√2.

problems.title: The part of a trapezoid midline between diagonals
problems.question: MN is a trapezoid midline;the diagonals meet it atP,Q. If PQ=1.2BC,find AD/BC.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: The segment between diagonal midpoints is(AD−BC)/2 in the pictured ordering.
steps: Thus(AD−BC)/2=1.2BC,so AD=3.4BC. The ratio is3.4.
problems.note: None of the printed choices4.6,2.5,3.2,2.8 equals the ratio forced by PQ=1.2BC.

problems.title: Domain of a nested radical fraction
problems.question: Find domain of √(3−√(25−x²))/(x²−3|x|).
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Require25−x²≥0,3−√(25−x²)≥0,and x²−3|x|≠0.
steps: The first two conditions give|x|≤5 and√(25−x²)≤3,so|x|≥4.
The excluded denominator roots0,±3 are already outside. Thus the domain is[−5,−4]∪[4,5].

problems.title: Range after a linear transform and absolute value
problems.question: f has range[−3,5]. Find range of g(x)=|2f(3x−1)−3|+1.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: As x varies over the transformed domain,3x−1 covers the domain of f. Thus2f−3 covers[−9,7].
steps: Taking absolute value gives[0,9],because the interval contains zero. Adding1 gives[1,10].

problems.title: Read slopes from a square grid
problems.question: Find tanABC from the supplied grid diagram.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: The grid gives AB rising1 for every4 horizontal units and BC rising2 for every1 horizontal unit. For direction vectors u,v,tanθ=(signed cross product)/(dot product).
steps: From B,take BA proportional to(−4,−1),BC proportional to(1,2).
Their dot product is−6 and cross-product magnitude is7. The angleABC is obtuse,so its tangent is7/(−6)=−7/6.

problems.title: A leg and its hypotenuse projection
problems.question: In right triangleACB,the altitude footH splits hypotenuseAB intoAH=9,HB=16. Find AC.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: $AC^2=AH\cdot AB$ by similarity of the altitude triangles.
steps: AB=25,so AC²=9·25=225 and AC=15.

problems.title: Three roots when one absolute-value pair collapses
problems.question: For which a does||x+4|−7|=a have exactly three roots?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: For a≥0,the inner absolute value must be7+a or7−a.
steps: For0<a<7,both are positive and give four roots. At a=7,the values are14 and0,giving two roots plus one root.
At a=0,there are only two distinct roots;for a>7,only the positive branch remains. Thus exactly three occurs at a=7.

problems.title: Reduce an expression using the root equation
problems.question: m is a root of x²−5x−11=0. Find(7−m)(m+2).
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: Expand:(7−m)(m+2)=5m+14−m². Substitution gives5m+14−5m−11=3.

problems.title: Recover two vectors from linear combinations
problems.question: a−2b=(−5,0),a+b=(4,3). Find cosine of their angle.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Subtract to get3b=(9,3),so b=(3,1),a=(1,2).
steps: Their dot product is5,and lengths are√10 and√5. Thus cosine=5/√50=1/√2.

problems.title: Square perimeter from an incircle circumference
problems.question: A square’s incircle has circumference9π. Find square perimeter.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: $2\pi r=9\pi$,so diameter2r=9.
steps: The square side equals the incircle diameter9. Its perimeter is4·9=36.

problems.title: Count integers between irrational roots
problems.question: How many integers solve−x²+3x+11≥0?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Boundary roots are(3±√53)/2,approximately−2.14 and5.14.
steps: The upward form x²−3x−11≤0 holds between them. The integers are−2,−1,0,1,2,3,4,5,eight in all.

problems.title: Check the zero-function exception to graph symmetry
problems.question: Which symmetry is impossible for a function graph:origin,Oy,Ox,or y=x?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Ox symmetry sends(x,y) to(x,−y). A function can have both only when y=0.
steps: A graph symmetric aboutOx must therefore be the zero function on its domain. Such a function does exist,so Ox symmetry is possible.
The other symmetries are also possible: y=x is symmetric about the origin and y=x itself; y=x² is symmetric aboutOy.
Hence none of the four symmetries is unconditionally impossible.
problems.answer: As written,none is impossible. Intended answer for a nonzero function graph:Ox.
problems.note: The printed question omits the exception of the zero function. A nonzero-value condition would make the intended answer correct.

problems.title: Choose the input giving the requested argument
problems.question: If f((x+3)/(1−x))=x/2,find f(3).
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Set(x+3)/(1−x)=3,withx≠1.
steps: Then x+3=3−3x,so x=0. The right side is0/2=0. Thus f(3)=0.

problems.title: Area from a line intersection inside a square
problems.question: E,F are midpoints of BC,CD in side-10 squareABCD. As in the diagram,AE and BF meet atP. Find area APFD.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: Lines AE and BF are y=2x and y=10−x/2. Their intersection isP=(4,8).
The shoelace formula for A,P,F,D gives area|4·5−8·10−5·10|/2=55.
problems.note: The text prints RF although R is undefined. The diagram clearly shows BF; this explanation uses that drawn segment.

problems.title: Reverse a homothety
problems.question: A homothety with centre(2,−1),factor−0.5 sends A toB(−3,5). Find A.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: $B-O=k(A-O)$,so $A=O+(B-O)/k$.
steps: B−O=(−5,6). Dividing by−1/2 gives(10,−12). Adding O givesA=(12,−13).

problems.title: A rational numerator may be zero
problems.question: Which is not necessarily true: rational+irrational is irrational;rational×rational is rational;irrational/rational is irrational;rational/irrational is irrational?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: $0/\sqrt2=0$,which is rational.
steps: Thus the last assertion is false in general. The first two assertions hold;the third holds for a nonzero rational denominator.
problems.answer: A rational divided by an irrational need not be irrational.
problems.note: Any quotient statement presumes a nonzero denominator; the third assertion otherwise has an additional undefined case.

problems.title: Intersection followed by distance to the origin
problems.question: Find distance from the intersection of y=4x−8 and3x−2y=1 to the origin.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Substitute y into the second equation;then use d=√(x²+y²).
steps: 3x−2(4x−8)=1 gives x=3. Then y=4. Distance=√(9+16)=5.

problems.title: A function equal to its inverse
problems.question: Which listed function equals its own inverse:2x−1,x²,√x,199/x?
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: A bijection is its own inverse when f(f(x))=x on its domain.
steps: For f(x)=199/x,on nonzero real inputs,f(f(x))=199/(199/x)=x.
Thus the reciprocal function is self-inverse.

problems.title: Angles in arithmetic progression
problems.question: A triangle’s angles form an arithmetic progression. Its middle-length side is4√3. Find circumradius.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: The middle angle is180°/3=60°. By the sine rule,a=2RsinA.
steps: The middle side is opposite the middle angle. Thus4√3=2R·√3/2=R√3,givingR=4.

problems.title: Length of an internal angle bisector
problems.question: In triangleABC,AB=12,BC=18,AD=6,DC=9. Find BD.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: AD/DC=AB/BC=2/3,so BD is an angle bisector; $BD^2=AB\cdot BC-AD\cdot DC$.
steps: This standard bisector identity givesBD²=216−54=162. Therefore BD=9√2.

problems.title: Symmetric pairs in an arithmetic progression
problems.question: The first10 terms of an arithmetic progression sum to35. Find a₃+a₈.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
steps: Thus the requested sum is35/5=7.

problems.title: Product of an odd number of geometric terms
problems.question: The sixth term of a geometric progression is4. Find product of its first11 terms.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: $a_i a_{12-i}=a_6^2$ for each of the five symmetric pairs.
steps: The product is(a₆²)⁵a₆=a₆¹¹=4¹¹=2²².

problems.title: Three arithmetic terms form a geometric progression
problems.question: An increasing arithmetic progression begins at2. Its second,seventh,twenty-seventh terms form a geometric progression. Find difference d.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: The terms are2+d,2+6d,2+26d;require(2+6d)²=(2+d)(2+26d).
steps: Expanding and subtracting gives10d²−30d=0,so d=0 or3.
Increasing means d>0,so d=3. The terms5,20,80 verify the geometric ratio4.

problems.title: Intersect two circles in a square
problems.question: In side-12 squareABCD,a circle centred atA with radiusAB meets the circle with diameterDC atE. Find ED.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: Use A=(0,0),D=(12,0),C=(12,12). The equations are x²+y²=144 and(x−12)²+(y−6)²=36.
steps: Subtract to obtain2x+y=24. Substituting y=24−2x into the first equation gives5x²−96x+432=0.
One intersection isD;the other isE=(36/5,48/5).

problems.title: Share-price ratio versus total company value
problems.question: 600000 GEL buys20% more B shares than A shares. Buying30% of each company costs7500000 GEL. Find A’s total share value.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: The price-per-share ratio is p_A/p_B=1.2. The second statement gives V_A+V_B=7500000/0.3=25000000.
steps: A price-per-share ratio alone does not give a total-value ratio without knowing the share counts.
For example,p_A=120,p_B=100 fits the first condition. Share counts100000,130000 give values12million,13million;counts125000,100000 give15million,10million. Both fit the second condition.
If equal total share counts were intended,then V_A=1.2V_B and V_A=(6/11)·25000000=150000000/11 GEL.
problems.answer: As written,not uniquely determined. With equal share counts:150000000/11≈13636363.64 GEL.
problems.note: The question needs equal total share counts,or a comparison of company ownership percentages purchasable,to justify the usual numerical answer.

problems.title: Shift both quadratic roots by two
problems.question: Find a for which roots of x²−(a³−3a²+6)x+3a−16=0 are2 larger than roots of x²−(a−1)x−a³+4a=0.
problems.idea: Read the stated conditions and diagram together,then simplify with the appropriate identity.
formulas: If second roots have sum S=a−1 and product P=−a³+4a,the shifted roots have sum S+4 and product P+2S+4.
steps: Equating sums givesa³−3a²+6=a+3,or(a−3)(a−1)(a+1)=0.
Equating products gives3a−16=−a³+6a+2,or a³−3a−18=0. Its factorisation is(a−3)(a²+3a+6),and the quadratic has no real roots.
Thus onlya=3 works. The second roots are−3,5;the first are−1,7,confirming the required shift.
